one_line: A shared map for negotiating group plans while keeping sensitive constraints private.
what_it_does: Lets participants and their agents add visible, private, or agent-only needs to a live planning room, eliminate unsuitable places, research missing facts, and converge on a venue or plan.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: agents can operate on shared live state and advocate using private user context without disclosing the underlying reason; ordinary UI-driving agents cannot replicate that privacy and synchronization comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and transcript describe shared live map state, agent negotiation, private constraints, and agent-only needs.
Transcript says private needs affect shared results without revealing the need or owner.
Frame sheets show a map-like collaborative workspace with participant markers, proposals, and constraints.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, unusually complete workflow from room setup through constraint handling, privacy, research, and proposal, with substantial frame and transcript evidence; some final flow is truncated and not directly observed.
execution_evidence: 174-second explainer transcript describes end-to-end room setup, invite, needs, privacy, deadlock resolution, research, and proposal.
Three frame sheets show branded entry states and collaborative map/card states.
Demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Groups routinely struggle to make decisions when preferences arrive asynchronously or include sensitive constraints; this directly addresses that problem with a credible shared decision process.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies scattered dietary, budget, timing, and private constraints as the core problem.
Transcript demonstrates privacy-preserving compromise and researching incomplete venue information.
creativity_rationale: The combination of live group decision modeling, private constraint effects, personal agent advocacy, and quantified ways out of deadlock is a memorable interaction model rather than a conventional group chat or search page.
creativity_evidence: Agent-only needs never reach the server while still informing the agent's advocacy.
The product exposes the cost of making a constraint optional and offers private exits when no option satisfies everyone.
Map/card visualization turns negotiation into a shared spatial model.
usability_note: The sparse onboarding and card/map presentation appear approachable, though frame text is small and the full interaction was not independently tested.
red_flags: The transcript is truncated before the complete closing workflow.
Most detailed behavior is claimed in text rather than independently observed.
standouts: Privacy-preserving agent advocacy in a multi-person decision.
Deadlock resolution modeled as explicit, private tradeoffs.
advance_reason: High-leverage, high-impact concept with strong end-to-end packet evidence and a distinctive collaboration model.

one_line: A contractor workday and photo-proof review app with agent-assisted handoff preparation.
what_it_does: Keeps job photos, completed work, and daily notes together; an agent checks records for missing information, suggests evidence, and prepares a printable or savable handoff for contractor approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured agent checks across job records and evidence can reduce review friction and improve repeatability, but a capable UI-driving agent could plausibly perform much of the same workflow with real, not fundamental, friction.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent checking records, finding missing information, and preparing updates for review.
Devpost screenshot shows photo-proof metadata, a passed check, and an explicit human confirmation step.
execution_rationale: The screenshot shows a coherent contractor/photo-proof surface and a review state, but there is no submitted video and the packet gives limited evidence of the complete save-and-handoff workflow.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets and Devpost screenshot show workday, attention items, photo proof, metadata, and review UI.
Demo is reported alive.
About text calls the app partial and describes handoff behavior without showing it end to end.
impact_rationale: Small contractors have a concrete need to document completed work and produce credible handoff records; the evidence-review workflow fits that audience directly.
impact_evidence: Title explicitly targets contractors.
Screenshot shows workday attention items, six photos, photo IDs, timestamps, and confirmation that evidence proves the work.
creativity_rationale: Agent-assisted photo evidence verification and handoff is a useful angle on contractor software, but the underlying job-record and approval category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Photo suggestion uses stored date, caption, ID, and work-time metadata.
Workflow combines check, correction, approval, and handoff.
usability_note: The visible review interface is understandable and approval-oriented, though completeness and responsive behavior are not established.
red_flags: No video submitted.
Author describes the app as partial; end-to-end handoff is not evidenced.
standouts: Concrete evidence-first contractor workflow.

advance_reason: Credible and useful, but evidence is thin and the WebMCP delta and novelty are moderate.

one_line: An approval-gated missed-call desk that stages cited rescue plans and editable replies.
what_it_does: Compares fictional missed calls against owner capacity, stages a cited rescue plan, lets the owner accept it, drafts an editable reply, and queues the current revision for review without sending.
leverage_rationale: The agent must compare multiple calls and constraints, cite exact records, and stage stateful work while approval boundaries prevent self-authorization; structured tools materially improve reliability over UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: Five named WebMCP tools expose inbox comparison, plan staging, lead inspection, drafting, and review queueing.
About text specifies stale edits cannot be queued and the agent cannot accept, approve, review, or send.
Agent-generated plan and draft appear in the same owner desk.
execution_rationale: The described state machine is intentional and safety-conscious, with a live demo and clear boundaries, but no video or frame evidence was submitted beyond packaging screenshots.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive.
About text enumerates owner actions, agent actions, reset behavior, and approval checkpoints.
Five fictional calls provide a defined scenario.
impact_rationale: Small service businesses lose revenue and responsiveness to missed calls; prioritizing limited follow-up capacity and preparing safe replies is a credible operational benefit.
impact_evidence: Use case centers on a detailing shop owner missing calls while working.
Workflow explicitly handles deadlines, job value, permissions, and a 30-minute capacity constraint.
creativity_rationale: The rescue-plan abstraction and explicit non-send approval architecture are a fresh, well-pursued take on an inbox assistant, though the business inbox category is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent stages but cannot accept its own plan or send.
Citations, revision freshness, and owner checkpoints are built into the interaction model.
usability_note: The staged-plan and editable-draft flow is operationally legible and conservative by design.
red_flags: No video frame sheets submitted despite packet listing none; visual execution cannot be fully checked.
Scenario uses fictional calls.
standouts: Strong approval and capability-boundary design.
Cited multi-call triage rather than generic reply generation.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP integration and credible safety/approval workflow justify advancing despite limited visual evidence.

leverage_rationale: Agents can inspect and manipulate canonical synth state precisely, then iterate against human auditory feedback; DOM-driving would be substantially less reliable for a dense audio instrument, though the outcome remains possible with effort.

impact_evidence: Author identifies hobbyist music-production use case and time lost searching for sounds.
Workflow supports listening, feedback, iteration, and export into production software.
creativity_rationale: Using an agent as a conversational sound-design collaborator, with a canonical patch model and live auditory iteration, is a fresh and ambitious interaction for WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent constructs a synth in the app from descriptions and revises it from user listening feedback.
Compiling a real open-source wavetable engine and exporting Vital format pursues the concept beyond a visual mockup.
usability_note: A compact visual synth and conversational iteration could be approachable, but the packet does not establish audio latency or export reliability.

standouts: Agent-human auditory feedback loop.

usability_note: The audit framing is legible, but no running screens establish report clarity or workflow usability.

Core functionality is evidenced primarily by description and packaging.

one_line: A collaborative architecture canvas that prices, audits, and compiles cloud designs with agents.

Agent can audit with citations, patch findings, and compile architecture code.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad but coherent system spanning canvas, live pricing sources, audits, multiplayer, imports/exports, and cdk synth compilation; three frame sheets and live demo support substantial claimed completion, though no video.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive; public repository exists.
Eight gallery images plus three frame sheets are submitted.
About text gives concrete implementation details including AWS Price List Bulk API, source URLs, cdk synth, CloudFormation, diagrams, and client-side operation.
impact_rationale: Cloud architects and engineering teams have a concrete need to align architecture, cost, documentation, and deployable output; integrating these artifacts can prevent expensive drift and rework.
impact_evidence: Product targets architecture design and costing in one shared workspace.
Claims real per-SKU pricing with sources, audits citing cloud documentation, and deployable compilation.
Multiplayer and Mermaid round-trip address collaboration and existing documentation.
creativity_rationale: The ambitious fusion of live priced architecture, agent-native semantic editing, self-audit, code compilation, and diagram round-tripping is unusually deep and memorable for a hackathon.
creativity_evidence: One document links visual design, cost numbers, audits, and infrastructure code.

Dynamic tool registration and abort-on-commit show attention to interaction architecture.

one_line: An isolated workbench that verifies whether WebMCP tools behave as declared.
what_it_does: Discovers a site's tools, reads schemas and annotations, generates synthetic inputs, invokes tools in a disposable browser, captures outputs and side effects, diffs state, and suggests repairs.
leverage_rationale: The product is specifically built around structured WebMCP discovery and invocation, with isolated execution and observable state/network evidence that ordinary UI-driving cannot reliably provide.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies tool discovery, schema/annotation inspection, safe input generation, isolated invocation, and before/after state comparison.
Workbench includes timeline, browser-state diff, network activity, and runtime logs.
ToolTruth exposes its own tools for inspecting and running verification.
execution_rationale: The workflow and evidence model are coherent and well specified, with live demo and frame sheets showing a workbench; actual verification depth is claimed rather than video-observed.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive; public repository exists.
Three frame sheets and three gallery images submitted.
About text details disposable browser, evidence timeline, diff, network, logs, and repair suggestion.
impact_rationale: WebMCP developers have a concrete reliability and trust problem: declared read-only or safe behavior may differ from actual side effects. Repeatable evidence can improve tool quality and user trust.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies tools that claim read-only behavior while changing state or making modifying requests.
Output compares claims with observable side effects and suggests repairs.
creativity_rationale: Treating WebMCP tools as test subjects and making their behavioral contract observable through isolated replay, diffs, and evidence is an original and well-pursued developer interaction.
creativity_evidence: Synthetic safe input generation plus disposable-browser verification is a distinctive workflow.
The tool exposes current-run inspection and focus capabilities to an external agent while a human follows along.
usability_note: A timeline/diff/log workbench is a sensible presentation for developers, though complexity and false-positive handling are not evidenced.
red_flags: No video submitted; actual side-effect capture and isolation are not directly demonstrated.
Synthetic input safety and coverage may be difficult across arbitrary tools.
standouts: Directly validates behavioral truth rather than tool descriptions.
Strong evidence-oriented workbench model.
advance_reason: High WebMCP indispensability and a credible, novel developer need with solid packet evidence.

creativity_evidence: OpenTelemetry baggage propagates product identity across project boundaries.
